guidelines.detail: refines EVT-03 (The description makes reaching the deadline, in competition with other possible outcomes, determine whether the process continues. The records show the corresponding catch event and flows are absent. This adds a specific application of the documented rule to wait for a trigger by identifying the timer and the competing-outcomes case.)

refines FID-01 (The description states communications with external participants, while the generated pools and message flows have no counterparts in the reference. The guideline gives concrete collaboration modeling guidance for FID-01’s broader requirement to model stated participants and messages.)

documentation rule EVT-01 not applied (The description identifies an initiating condition before the first activity, while the reference start event and its flow are absent from the generated model. No extra-element record suggests the trigger was modeled using another BPMN element. Documented guideline EVT-01 already says to use start events for stated process triggers.)

same as LRN-046 (The description explicitly includes sending a request, receiving money or a disagreement, and forwarding a case to external parties. The generated pools and message flows represent these interactions, while the reference omits them. The wording is general and matches learned guideline LRN-046.)

same as LRN-045 (The description makes reaching the deadline a condition for continuing, and the records show the deadline event and its flows are absent. The learned guideline LRN-045 already states essentially the same modeling rule.)

same as LRN-046 (The description states exchanges with external parties, so the generated pools and message flows are supported; their absence from the reference does not justify omitting them, and doing so would conflict with COL-01. This guideline is already essentially covered by LRN-046.)

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says that reaching a deadline can determine which continuation occurs, while other outcomes may also occur first: Model the wait for the deadline as a timer intermediate catch event, using an event-based gateway when the deadline competes with other catching outcomes.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that reaching a deadline can determine which continuation occurs, while other outcomes may also occur first

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that an internal process sends information or an item to an external participant, or receives information or an item from one: Model the external participant as a separate pool and represent the stated communications with message flows.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that an internal process sends information or an item to an external participant, or receives information or an item from one

rules_sent_back.instruction: Use start events for stated process triggers. A start event has no incoming sequence flow and is not the source of a message flow.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states a trigger that initiates the process before its first activity
